title: Overhaul minor hydraulic components on agricultural equipment

lessons.title: Minor hydraulic parts and safe preparation
lessons.html:
Which parts are minor hydraulic components?

Minor hydraulic parts are the smaller parts you can overhaul in the farm workshop. Examples are:

  • hydraulic cylinders (rams) on loaders, tipper trailers, planters and ploughs;
  • quick-release couplers;
  • hydraulic hoses and fittings;
  • simple control valves and check valves on implements;
  • hydraulic filters and strainers.

Big parts like the main pump and the tractor lift unit usually go to a specialist. Ask your supervisor if you are not sure.

Why overhaul?

A leaking ram wastes oil, makes a mess and lets the load drop slowly. A seal kit costs much less than a new ram. Overhauling on time also stops dirt getting into the whole tractor hydraulic system.

Safety

  • Lower the implement or loader to the ground, or block it up on strong stands. Never work under a load held up only by hydraulics.
  • Switch off the engine and move the control levers back and forth to release pressure.
  • Uncouple hoses only after the pressure is released.
  • Hydraulic oil under pressure can go through skin. This is a medical emergency – get to a doctor at once.
  • Never check for leaks with your hand. Use cardboard.
  • Wear gloves and safety glasses.
  • Catch oil in drip trays and keep used oil for recycling. Oil spills poison soil and water.

lessons.title: Overhauling a hydraulic cylinder
lessons.html:
Removing the cylinder

  1. Clean the outside, especially around hose fittings.
  2. Tag the hoses and note which port each goes to.
  3. Disconnect the hoses and cap them and the cylinder ports right away.
  4. Support the cylinder, remove the pins and lift it out.

Dismantling

  1. Drain the oil into a tray by moving the rod in and out by hand.
  2. Clamp the barrel in a vice with soft jaws. Do not squeeze it out of round.
  3. Undo the gland nut with the correct spanner, or remove the circlip.
  4. Pull the rod and piston out slowly and straight.
  5. Remove the piston nut and slide off the piston and gland.
  6. Remove all old seals with a plastic or brass pick. Steel picks scratch the grooves.

Checking

PartCheck
RodStraight, chrome not pitted, rusty or scratched
BarrelNo scoring or rust inside
Piston and glandNo cracks, grooves clean
Eye ends and pinsBushes not worn oval

A bent or badly pitted rod must be replaced or rechromed by a specialist. A scored barrel will quickly ruin new seals.

Reassembling

  • Fit the new seal kit for that cylinder. Match each new seal to the old one.
  • Wet seals with clean hydraulic oil.
  • Protect seals from sharp threads with tape or a fitting sleeve.
  • Tighten the piston nut and gland to the manual torque.

lessons.title: Hoses, couplers, refitting and testing
lessons.html:
Hoses

Replace a hose if it has:

  • a cracked or worn outer cover showing the wire inside;
  • a bulge or blister;
  • leaking or rusted end fittings;
  • kinks or flat spots.

Use a new hose of the same pressure rating, size and length. Many farm suppliers make up hoses. Take the old hose with you. Fit hoses so they do not twist or rub on sharp edges, and leave enough length for the implement to move.

Quick couplers

  • Keep dust caps on couplers when not connected. Dirt in a coupler goes straight into the tractor oil.
  • Wipe both halves clean before connecting.
  • A leaking or sticking coupler can be fitted with a new seal kit or replaced.

Refitting and testing

  1. Fit the cylinder, fit the pins and new split pins or bolts.
  2. Connect hoses to the right ports using your tags.
  3. Start the engine at low speed and work the ram in and out slowly several times to push out air.
  4. Check and top up the tractor hydraulic oil with the type in the manual.
  5. Lift a normal load and hold it. It must not sink.
  6. Check for leaks with cardboard.

Record the parts used and the test on the job card.

Key points

  • Lower or block loads and release pressure before you start.
  • Keep everything clean and cap all open ports and hoses.
  • Use plastic or brass picks for seals and fit the correct seal kit.
  • Replace hoses with the same pressure rating, size and length.
  • Bleed out air and test that the ram holds a load without leaking.
